scope: Opt-in remote desktop transport to one persistent Runtime Host; existing local mode preserved

backend_full_suite.note: Full suite before final shutdown and handshake edge-case additions; final affected tests rerun separately

cases: Two desktop clients share server session history
Accepted turn completes after requester disconnects; no automatic retransmission
Real Calendar MCP creates one todo on Host; second desktop reads it
Host restart preserves root identity, rotates epoch, and restores sessions and todos
Connected client automatically reconnects without replaying model calls
Visible remote connection status, server model, local-only features disabled
Actual Electron composer invokes real Host and Calendar MCP
Host stop displays disconnection; restart restores connection and the selected history
Exactly one server execution and one todo after restart
No local Python child, config.toml, sessions.db, or execution database in remote desktop profile

configuration.verification: config.toml, channels.json, mcp_servers.json and proactive_sources.json SHA-256 hashes match the pre-work snapshot
configuration.production_local_mode: Existing Kaze bridge remains running and healthy; no production switch to remote mode

boundaries: Real network transport is tested on loopback, including a visible Electron client; no public server/TLS proxy deployment
Model responses are deterministic offline fixtures; Calendar MCP, AgentLoop and persistence are real
No live Telegram test message in this phase; external channel commit propagation covered by regression
Remote mode supports text sessions, history, execution records, workbench and Host-side tools; local file upload, voice, pet and configuration editing are not exposed
Single-user shared token, no multi-tenant authorization or offline write queue
Host crash recovery uses the existing durable execution journal and does not automatically replay unfinished side effects
